title: Email, connectors, and moving between chats
notes: Email has an Inbox and a Sent list. Sent mail loads reliably, and says so when it did not load, instead of waiting forever.
The email reader shows a message the way the sender made it, with pictures.
Replies can carry files and photos. Redraft shows that it is working.
Add to Calendar reads the whole thread and shows you the exact event before it adds anything.
Connectors has a search field, and the Add list now shows Anthropic's full directory of about 300 connectors.
Swipe left or right in a chat to move to the next or previous chat.
A chat names itself after its first reply. Swipe right on any chat to name it by hand.
An agent can schedule a later check inside its own chat, so "look at this tomorrow" actually happens.
Settings has a Sources section. Your vault, email, texts and calendar each come from the machine you pick, one at a time.
HomeADE reaches your other machines, such as a work laptop, through the relay. Pair one by pasting its pairing link.
Texts stay in sync. Deleting a group chat goes through Messages, and changes the Mac cannot make yet wait in a queue.
Fixed crashes at launch, when opening a chat, and when swiping between chats. A failed connection test now says what went wrong and what to do.

title: First release as HomeADE
notes: The Mac window and the menu-bar app are now one app. It was called Home Base; it is now HomeADE.
It talks to this Mac directly. It no longer keeps a list of home bases or relays to itself.
Paste a screenshot or a copied image into a chat with ⌘V.
The + button opens the model list at once.
A Connectors section in the sidebar lists the tools your assistants can reach, with counts of the ones working and failing.
Send to agent on an email or a text opens a chat with the whole thread.
Fixed: saving a setting could erase the end-to-end key and cause a 403 after pairing.

title: First public release, then called Home Base
notes: One Mac app: a window with the same screens as the phone, a menu-bar panel, and the home base that runs your assistants.
Signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens without a warning. Install with a download or with Homebrew.
